title: Anthropic Just Made Thousands of Workers Millionaires. Here's How
sources: Thousands of millionaires: CNBC headline 'Anthropic IPO will create thousands of multimillionaire employees' (Nov 19 2026); NY Post via Yahoo: about 2,800 staff worth at least $10M.
IPO: priced at $83 a share, Nasdaq debut Nov 19 2026, closed $97.17 (Forbes, Yahoo Finance, CNN).
Employees: about 5,300 (SEC filings via CNBC); stakes about $232 billion at $83, about $44 million each on average (CNBC calculation from filing share counts; also Fortune).
Options: about 1.77 billion stock options with a strike price of $2.91 (SEC filings via CNBC).
Co-founders: seven, each about $20 billion at $83 (CNBC from SEC filings; CBS News).
Selling: employees may sell up to 10% once trading begins (Yahoo Finance / NY Post; Fortune), another 35% after earnings (Fortune).

lines.text: Anthropic, the AI company, just turned thousands of its workers into millionaires.
Here's how. As part of their pay, many workers got the right to buy company shares for about three dollars each.
This week, the company started selling shares to the public, for eighty-three dollars each.
On average, each worker now owns about forty-four million dollars in stock.
And the seven people who started the company? About twenty billion dollars each.
But there's a catch. For now, workers can sell only ten percent of their shares.
So if a job ever offers you stock instead of cash, ask two things. How much do I pay? And when can I sell?
Cash or stock? Which would you pick?
